title: Jain Udad Dal + Rice (PIP, 1 Person)
instructions: Step 1 — Gather tools: Instant Pot, trivet, 1 steel bowl (for rice), measuring spoons/cups, spatula, ladle.
Step 2 — Measure & rinse: Measure dal and rice. Rinse each separately until water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Step 3 — Assemble rice bowl: In a steel bowl add rice, 1 cup water, 1 tsp ghee, 1/2 tsp jeeru, 1/4 tsp salt; stir and set aside.
Step 4 — Temper dal: IP on Saute (Normal). Add 2 tsp oil/ghee. When hot, add rai to crackle (5–10 sec), then hing, turmeric, red chilli; stir 5–10 sec without burning.
Step 5 — Start dal base: Add rinsed udad dal, 1 1/4 cups water, 1/2 tsp salt; stir, then press Cancel to exit Saute.
Step 6 — PIP assembly: Place trivet directly into dal in the inner pot. Set the rice bowl on the trivet; ensure it sits level. Close lid; set valve to Sealing.
Step 7 — Pressure cook: Pressure Cook — High: 9 minutes.
Step 8 — Release: Allow Natural Release for 3–4 minutes; then carefully Quick Release remaining pressure. Open lid away from you.
Step 9 — Finish textures: Fluff rice with fork. Stir dal; if too thick, add hot water 1–2 tbsp at a time; if thin, Saute (Low) 2–3 minutes to reduce, stirring.
Step 10 — Taste & serve: Adjust salt/heat. Serve dal hot with jeera rice. Optional ghee drizzle on rice.

title: Sweet Rice Water Osaman (No Sauté)
ingredients: Leftover cooked rice water – 1.5 to 2 cups (strained)
Black salt or regular salt – tiny pinch (optional)
instructions: Step 1 — Collect base: After boiling rice, strain and save the thin starchy water (osaman). Remove any grains.
Step 2 — Set up pot: Use a small saucepan or IP on Saute (Low). Add the rice water.
Step 3 — Warm gently: Heat until steaming but not boiling to avoid a raw starchy taste.
Step 4 — Sweeten: Stir in 1–2 tsp sugar to taste; dissolve fully. Add a tiny pinch of black salt or regular salt if desired.
Step 5 — Serve: Pour into a cup and serve warm, as a light sweet broth.

title: Jain Pink Sauce Pasta (Less Watery, with Butter & Cheese)
instructions: Step 1 — Prep slurry: In a cup, whisk milk and cornstarch until lump-free; set aside.
Step 2 — Build masala base: IP Saute (Normal); add 1 tsp oil + 1 tbsp butter. Crackle rai (5–10 sec), add hing, then red chilli, sabji masala, jeeru masala; toast 5–10 sec.
Step 3 — Tomato-sweet balance: Stir in ketchup and optional sugar; cook ~30 seconds until slightly darker and aromatic.
Step 4 — Coat pasta: Add dry elbow pasta; toss 20–30 sec to coat in masala-fat so it won’t stick.
Step 5 — Pressure cook: Add 1 cup water and salt; Cancel Saute. Lid on, valve Sealing. Pressure Cook — High: 5 minutes; Quick Release immediately.
Step 6 — Reduce excess liquid (if any): If watery, Saute (Low) 30–60 sec, stirring, until saucy.
Step 7 — Make it pink: With Saute (Low) on, pour in the milk–cornstarch slurry in a thin stream while stirring constantly. Simmer 2–3 min until it thickly coats the pasta.
Step 8 — Cheesy finish: Add cheese; stir to melt. Add 1 tsp butter for gloss. Adjust salt/sugar.
Step 9 — Brighten & serve: Switch off; add a few drops of lemon juice. Rest 1 minute; serve thick and creamy.

title: Cheese Butter Masala (Jain Style, 1 Serving)
instructions: Step 1 — Prep dairy: Whisk milk and cornstarch until smooth; set aside.
Step 2 — Start base: Pan/IP Saute (Normal). Add 1 tsp oil + 1/2 tbsp butter. Crackle rai, then hing.
Step 3 — Cook tomatoes: Add chopped tomatoes, pinch salt, turmeric, and half the red chilli; cook 6–7 min stirring until soft and glossy.
Step 4 — Blend: Switch off; cool 1–2 min; blend to a smooth puree (immersion blender or jar).
Step 5 — Return & season: Pour puree back; add sabji masala, garam masala, sugar; stir.
Step 6 — Thicken gently: Saute (Low). Slowly add milk–cornstarch slurry while stirring; simmer 3–4 min until creamy. Adjust salt.
Step 7 — Add cheese: Add cheese cubes; simmer 2–3 min just to soften (do not overcook).
Step 8 — Finish: Stir in remaining 1/2 tbsp butter for shine; switch off; add lemon juice. Rest 1 min and serve.

title: Jain Tomato Soup (2 Tomatoes, 1 Serving)
ingredients: Butter – 1 tbsp (1/2 for cooking, 1/2 for finishing)
Cornstarch – 1/2 tsp (mix into milk for slurry)
Cheese cube (optional) – 1, grated or dropped in
instructions: Step 1 — Make slurry: Whisk milk and cornstarch until smooth; set aside.
Step 2 — Temper: In a saucepan melt 1/2 tbsp butter; crackle rai; add hing.
Step 3 — Cook tomatoes: Add chopped tomatoes, pinch salt, and optional chilli; cook 6–8 min on medium until pulpy and glossy.
Step 4 — Blend: Cool 1–2 min; blend smooth (strain if you prefer a silky texture).
Step 5 — Simmer base: Return puree to pot; add 1 cup water, sugar, and salt; simmer 3–4 min.
Step 6 — Creamy finish: On Low heat, drizzle in the milk–cornstarch slurry while stirring; simmer 2–3 min until lightly thickened.
Step 7 — Finish & serve: Stir in remaining 1/2 tbsp butter; optional grated cheese. Off heat add a few drops lemon; serve hot.

title: Jeera Rice (PIP Bowl, 1 Person)
instructions: Step 1 — Rinse rice: Wash rice in several changes of water until mostly clear; drain well.
Step 2 — Assemble bowl: In a steel bowl combine rice, 1 cup water, ghee/butter, jeeru, salt; stir.
Step 3 — PIP setup: Place trivet in IP inner pot over 1 cup water OR set over a base dish you are pressure cooking.
Step 4 — Pressure cook: Place rice bowl on trivet; lid on; valve Sealing. Pressure Cook — High: 8–10 min when paired with dal/beans, OR 4 min if cooking rice alone.
Step 5 — Release & fluff: Natural Release 5 min; then Quick Release. Fluff with fork and serve.

title: Jain Moong Dal (for PIP Combo, 1 Person)
instructions: Step 1 — Rinse & ready: Rinse dal until water runs clearer; drain. Measure water and spices.
Step 2 — Temper: IP Saute (Normal); add oil/ghee. Crackle rai; add hing and turmeric; stir 5 sec.
Step 3 — Start cook: Add moong dal, 1 1/4 cups water, and salt; stir and Cancel Saute.
Step 4 — Pressure cook: Pressure Cook — High: 8 min; Natural Release: 5 min; Quick Release.
Step 5 — Finish: Stir; thin with hot water if needed or reduce briefly on Saute (Low). Taste salt and serve.

title: Jain Sweet Kadhi (Milk-Based, 1 Serving)
ingredients: Lemon juice – 1 to 2 tsp (add off heat)
instructions: Step 1 — Slurry: In a bowl whisk milk, water, and cornstarch until smooth; set aside.
Step 2 — Temper: Pan/IP Saute (Normal); add ghee. Crackle rai, then add hing, turmeric, and optional chilli; stir 5 sec.
Step 3 — Add slurry: Lower to Saute (Low). Slowly pour in the slurry while stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
Step 4 — Season & simmer: Add salt, sugar, and jeeru masala; simmer gently 5–6 min, avoiding a hard boil.
Step 5 — Finish: Switch off; add lemon juice to taste (sweet–tang balance). Serve hot.

title: Mixed Small Pulses + Rice (PIP, 10-Min Version)
ingredients: Mixed small pulses (no chana/vatana) – 1/3 cup, rinsed
instructions: Step 1 — Rinse: Wash pulses and rice separately; drain well.
Step 2 — Temper pulses: IP Saute (Normal); add oil/ghee. Crackle rai; add hing, turmeric, red chilli, sabji/jeeru masala; stir 5 sec.
Step 3 — Start pulses: Add pulses + 1 1/4 cups water + 1/2 tsp salt; stir; Cancel Saute.
Step 4 — Rice bowl: In a steel bowl mix rice + 1 cup water + butter/ghee + jeeru + 1/4 tsp salt.
Step 5 — PIP assembly: Place trivet in pulses; set rice bowl on trivet; close lid; valve Sealing.
Step 6 — Pressure cook: Pressure Cook — High: 10 min; Natural Release: 10 min; Quick Release.
Step 7 — Finish: Fluff rice. Stir pulses; adjust thickness with reserved liquid or reduce on Saute (Low). Serve together.

title: Matki–Paneer Curry (IP Base, 1 Person)
instructions: Step 1 — Temper: IP Saute (Normal); add oil/ghee. Crackle rai; add hing, turmeric, red chilli, sabji masala; stir 5 sec.
Step 2 — Start matki: Add rinsed matki + 1 1/4 cups water + 1/2 tsp salt; stir; Cancel Saute.
Step 3 — Pressure cook: Pressure Cook — High: 12 min; Natural Release: 10 min; Quick Release.
Step 4 — Adjust: Saute (Low) 2–3 min to reach desired thickness.
Step 5 — Finish: Add paneer cubes; simmer 2 min. Stir in 1/2 tsp butter; serve.

title: Paneer Curry (Jain Masala Style, Quick)
instructions: Step 1 — Sear paneer: Pan/IP Saute (Normal); heat ghee/oil. Lightly saute paneer cubes 2–3 min; remove to a plate.
Step 2 — Bloom spices: Same pan; add hing, then red chilli, sabji masala, jeeru masala; stir 5–10 sec.
Step 3 — Build gravy: Add 1/2 cup water + salt; simmer 2 min. Optional: add milk + cornstarch slurry; simmer 2–3 min until lightly thick.
Step 4 — Finish: Return paneer; simmer 2 min. Off heat add lemon juice; optional 1/2 tsp butter for shine; serve.

title: Paneer Butter Masala (Jain, Tomato, 1 Person)
instructions: Step 1 — Slurry: Whisk milk and cornstarch until smooth; set aside.
Step 2 — Start base: Pan/IP Saute (Normal); add 1 tsp oil + 1/2 tbsp butter. Optional: crackle rai; add hing.
Step 3 — Cook tomatoes: Add chopped tomatoes, pinch salt, turmeric, and some red chilli; cook 5–6 min until soft.
Step 4 — Blend: Cool slightly; blend to a smooth puree.
Step 5 — Season gravy: Return puree; add sabji masala, garam masala, sugar, and salt; simmer 2–3 min.
Step 6 — Thicken gently: On Low heat, add the milk–cornstarch slurry slowly, stirring; simmer 3–4 min until creamy.
Step 7 — Add paneer: Add paneer cubes; simmer 2–3 min to heat through.
Step 8 — Finish: Stir in remaining 1/2 tbsp butter; off heat add lemon juice. Rest 1 min; serve with bread.

title: Green Vatana Curry (No Overnight Soak, Jain)
ingredients: Green vatana (dried whole green peas) – 1/2 cup, rinsed well
Water – 2 cups (for pressure cooking; add more if needed)
Paneer or cheese cube – optional (for richness at the end)
instructions: Step 1 — Rinse peas: Wash green vatana thoroughly; drain.
Step 2 — Pressure cook peas: Add peas to IP with 2 cups water and 1/2 tsp salt. Pressure Cook — High: 35–40 min; allow full Natural Release (15–20 min).
Step 3 — Check doneness: Peas should mash between fingers. If still firm, add 1/2 cup water and cook +10 min (High).
Step 4 — Adjust liquid: Drain excess cooking liquid if very watery, reserving some to thin later.
Step 5 — Temper: Saute (Normal); heat 1 tsp oil. Crackle rai; add hing, turmeric, red chilli, sabji masala; stir 5 sec.
Step 6 — Combine & simmer: Add peas and a ladle of reserved liquid; simmer 5–10 min to desired thickness, stirring.
Step 7 — Finish & balance: Stir in sugar; adjust salt. Off heat add lemon juice; swirl in 1 tsp butter and optional cheese/paneer cube. Serve hot.

title: Whole Moong Beans (Jain, No Overnight Soak)
ingredients: Whole moong beans – 1/3 cup, rinsed thoroughly
instructions: Step 1 — Rinse moong: Wash whole moong beans thoroughly 3–4 times until water runs mostly clear. Drain well.
Step 2 — Pressure cook: Add moong + 1 1/4 cups water + turmeric to the Instant Pot. Pressure Cook — High: 20 minutes (no soak) + Natural Release 10 minutes.
Step 3 — Check texture: Beans should be soft enough to mash easily between fingers. If slightly firm, add 1/4 cup water and cook +5 minutes (High).
Step 4 — Temper: Set IP to Saute (Normal). Add oil/ghee. Crackle rai (5–10 sec), add hing, red chilli (optional), sabji masala; stir 5 seconds.
Step 5 — Combine: Add cooked moong + salt; stir well. Simmer 3–4 minutes to thicken or reduce to preferred consistency.
Step 6 — Finish: Add sugar (optional) for flavor balance, swirl in butter, and turn off heat. Add lemon juice at the end before serving.

title: Khakhra Pizza (Jain Style)
ingredients: Pav Bhaji masala – tiny pinch (optional, adds depth)
instructions: Step 1 — Base: Place khakhra on a microwave-safe plate or flat pan.
Step 2 — Sauce: Mix ketchup + a tiny pinch pav bhaji masala (optional) + a sprinkle of salt; spread evenly over khakhra.
Step 3 — Butter: Dot or lightly spread softened butter on top for flavor and crispness.
Step 4 — Cheese: Sprinkle grated cheese evenly across the top.
Step 5 — Herbs: Sprinkle mixed herbs and chili flakes over the cheese.
Step 6 — Melt: Microwave 30–45 seconds until cheese just melts (or cover pan with lid for 1–2 min on low heat).
Step 7 — Serve: Cut into quarters, serve immediately while warm and crisp.

title: Masala Cheese Bread Toast (Jain Style)
ingredients: Cheese slices or grated cheese – 2 slices / 1 cube
Pav Bhaji masala or Shahi Paneer masala – small pinch (optional twist)
instructions: Step 1 — Prepare spread: Mix ketchup, red chilli powder, jeeru masala, and a small pinch of pav bhaji or shahi paneer masala to make a quick spiced sauce.
Step 2 — Toast base: Heat pan on medium-low. Butter one side of each bread slice and place buttered side down to toast until golden.
Step 3 — Assemble: Flip slices, spread spiced ketchup on the toasted side, top with cheese, and sprinkle herbs and chili flakes.
Step 4 — Cover cook: Reduce heat to low, cover pan with lid, and cook 1–2 min until cheese melts fully.
Step 5 — Serve: Slice diagonally and serve hot with extra ketchup or mint powder sprinkle.

title: Macaroni (Jain Basic Red Sauce Style)
instructions: Step 1 — Cook pasta: Add macaroni + 1 cup water + 1/2 tsp salt to Instant Pot. Pressure Cook — High: 5 minutes; Quick Release.
Step 2 — Drain excess water if needed and keep aside.
Step 3 — Temper: Sauté → Normal; add 1/2 tbsp butter; crackle rai, add hing, chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, jeeru masala, sabji masala. Stir 5 seconds.
Step 4 — Sauce: Add ketchup + sugar + 2 tbsp water. Mix until glossy.
Step 5 — Combine: Add cooked macaroni; mix to coat evenly. Add remaining butter for gloss.
Step 6 — Garnish: Sprinkle mixed herbs and chili flakes. Add few drops lemon juice before serving.

title: Mac & Cheese (Jain Creamy White Sauce Style)
ingredients: Cornstarch – 1/2 tsp (mix into milk as slurry)
Pav Bhaji masala – tiny pinch (optional fusion twist)
instructions: Step 1 — Cook macaroni: Add macaroni + 1 cup water + pinch salt to Instant Pot. Pressure Cook — High: 5 minutes; Quick Release.
Step 2 — Drain excess water if needed; keep pasta aside.
Step 3 — Sauce base: Set Sauté → Low. Melt butter in pot.
Step 4 — Add milk-cornstarch slurry slowly, stirring continuously until thick and creamy (~2 minutes).
Step 5 — Add grated cheese; stir until melted and smooth.
Step 6 — Season with salt, pepper, and (optional) mixed herbs, chili flakes, or pav bhaji masala for fusion flavor.
Step 7 — Combine: Add macaroni into sauce; mix to coat well. Serve hot and creamy.

title: Atta Nankhatai (Wheat Cookies, Jain)
instructions: Step 1 — Mix dry: In a bowl, combine atta, powdered sugar, cardamom, salt, and optional baking soda.
Step 2 — Add ghee: Mix in ghee gradually until dough just holds together. It should be soft but not sticky.
Step 3 — Shape: Roll small balls, flatten slightly. Place on parchment or greased tray.
Step 4 — Bake: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F). Bake 15–18 minutes until light golden at edges.
Step 5 — Cool: Let rest 10 minutes before moving. Store airtight once fully cool.

title: Chocolate Atta Cookies (Using Cold Cocoa Mix)
instructions: Step 1 — Combine: Mix atta, cocoa mix, sugar, salt, and optional baking soda in a bowl.
Step 2 — Add ghee/butter: Mix to form a soft dough. If dry, add 1 tbsp milk.
Step 3 — Shape: Make small cookies and flatten slightly.
Step 4 — Bake: Preheat oven to 160°C (320°F). Bake 12–15 minutes until edges firm.
Step 5 — Cool: Let cool completely for a crunchy texture.

title: Atta Tart Shells & Chocolate Tart (Jain, Eggless)
ingredients: Chocolate or Cold Cocoa Mix – 1 tbsp (extra for filling)
instructions: Step 1 — Shell dough: Combine atta, sugar, and ghee; mix until crumbly. Add milk slowly to form firm dough.
Step 2 — Shape: Press into small tart molds or cupcake liners (thin layer).
Step 3 — Bake shells: 160°C (320°F) for 12–15 minutes until light golden. Cool completely.
Step 4 — Filling: In a small pan, add milk + cornstarch slurry + butter + sugar + cocoa mix. Stir on low until thick and glossy.
Step 5 — Assemble: Spoon warm chocolate filling into tart shells. Chill 20–30 minutes to set. Serve cool.

title: Aate ka Sheera (Atta Halwa, Jain)
ingredients: Cashews or nuts (optional, Jain-safe roasted) – 1 tsp
instructions: Step 1 — Roast atta: Heat ghee in a pan. Add atta and roast on medium-low, stirring continuously, until golden brown and aromatic (6–8 minutes).
Step 2 — Add water: In a separate bowl, boil water. Slowly pour hot water into roasted atta while stirring constantly (it will bubble).
Step 3 — Sweeten: Add sugar and continue stirring until dissolved and mixture thickens.
Step 4 — Finish: Add cardamom powder, mix well, and cook 1–2 more minutes until ghee separates slightly.
Step 5 — Serve warm, optionally garnished with roasted nuts.

title: Atta Ladoo (Wheat Flour Sweet Balls, Jain)
ingredients: Cashew or almond pieces (optional, roasted) – 1 tsp
instructions: Step 1 — Roast: Heat ghee in pan, add atta, and roast on low-medium heat until golden brown and fragrant (6–8 min).
Step 2 — Cool slightly: Remove from heat, let cool 3–4 minutes (still warm).
Step 3 — Add sugar and cardamom; mix thoroughly.
Step 4 — Shape: While mixture is warm and pliable, shape into small ladoos. If dry, add 1–2 tsp melted ghee.
Step 5 — Set: Let cool fully; store airtight up to a week.
